# ASC 842 — Leases

**Issuer:** FASB (US GAAP)  
**Language:** EN  
**Topic:** lessee accounting for right-of-use assets

## Overview

ASC 842 requires lessees to recognize a **right-of-use (ROU) asset** and a
**lease liability** on the balance sheet for most leases with a term greater
than 12 months.

## Initial measurement

- Lease liability = present value of unpaid lease payments, discounted using
  the rate implicit in the lease if readily determinable, otherwise the
  lessee's incremental borrowing rate.
- ROU asset = lease liability adjusted for initial direct costs, prepaid rent,
  and lease incentives.

## Classification

- **Finance lease** — ownership transfers, purchase option reasonably certain,
  lease term is major part of economic life, or PV of payments substantially
  all of fair value.
- **Operating lease** — all other leases; expense generally recognized on a
  straight-line basis.

## Short-term exemption

Lessees may elect not to recognize ROU assets and liabilities for leases with
a term of 12 months or less that do not include a purchase option reasonably
certain to be exercised.
